battle.name: 第一次蘇丹內戰
battle.theater: 蘇丹南部赤道省與上尼羅河省
battle.brief: 1955年8月18日，赤道軍團第二連在托里特起兵，南北方對抗近十七年，直到1972年《亞的斯亞貝巴協定》才劃下臨時界線。卡面這具M3斯圖亞特輕型坦克並未在蘇丹成建制出現，南部叢林裡奔馳的是英制輪式裝甲車與裝甲列車；M3代表的正是同一世代以輕型裝甲承擔偵察護路的典型角色。

kit.name: M3 斯圖亞特輕型坦克
kit.history: M3 Stuart為二戰期間廣泛使用的輕型坦克，具備高速機動與可靠火力，主要用於偵察、快速突破及支援步兵，是美國裝甲兵力的骨幹之一。

countries: 第一次蘇丹內戰自1955年8月18日起，到1972年3月27日《亞的斯亞貝巴協定》簽署為止，交戰的兩極是北方的蘇丹國家機器與南方的分離主義武裝。1955至1956年間，蘇丹仍處在英埃共管之下：英國與埃及王國共同管治北部，南蘇丹則由英國殖民當局直接統治，總督為亞歷山大·諾克斯·赫爾姆（Alexander Knox Helm）；英軍在南蘇丹駐紮，蘇丹國防軍（Sudan Defence Force）由英方訓練與裝備，裝備與編制皆出英制體系。1956年1月蘇丹獨立後，北方成立以伊斯梅爾·阿扎里（Ismail al-Azhari）為總理的共和國，1958年軍事政變後軍人政權上台，1969年5月25日加法爾·尼米里（Gaafar Nimeiry）推翻民政當局，成立民主共和國。北方的軍隊即由蘇丹國防軍改組而成的蘇丹武裝部隊：1955年全軍僅約六千至七千人，到1971年底增至約三萬六千人，四個步兵旅中的一個自1955年起常駐赤道省，境內另有民兵性質的地方防衛隊；英軍顧問團一直留到1960年代中期，埃及部隊在1956年之前參與南部作戰，1969年起利比亞提供武器與經費，1970年更直接介入戰鬥，烏干達則在1965至1969年間允許南方武裝在本土活動並提供補給。南方一方的陣容更雜：由1955年托里特兵變的散兵起家的游擊隊1963年起成型，其名號「阿尼亞尼亞」（Anyanya，源自馬迪語，意思為蛇毒）後來成了整場戰爭的代稱，另有1965至1970年間活動的「阿札尼亞解放陣線」（ALF）等分裂武裝，以及各地方武裝團體；1969年起以色列亦直接介入，向南方陣線供應武器並派駐軍事顧問。戰場地理上，主要交鋒地帶是南部的赤道省（托里特、朱巴、耶伊、馬里迪）、上尼羅河省與巴赫爾加扎勒省，多為白尼羅河與其支流間的沼澤、叢林與雨林地帶。
countriesEn: The First Sudanese Civil War ran from 18 August 1955 to 27 March 1972, the date of the Addis Ababa Agreement, and pitted the northern Sudanese state against southern separatist armed groups. From 1955 to 1956 Sudan was still under Anglo-Egyptian condominium: Britain and the Kingdom of Egypt jointly governed the north, while the south was under direct British colonial administration with the governor-general Alexander Knox Helm; British troops were stationed in the southern Sudan, and the Sudan Defence Force was trained, organised and equipped on the British model. After independence in January 1956 the north set up a republic under Prime Minister Ismail al-Azhari; a military coup followed in 1958, and on 25 May 1969 Gaafar Nimeiry overthrew the civilian government and proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Sudan. The northern army was the Sudan Defence Force reconstituted as the Sudanese Armed Forces: about 6,000 to 7,000 men in 1955, rising to some 36,000 by late 1971, with one of the army's four infantry brigades stationed in Equatoria Province from 1955 onwards, alongside locally raised defence force and militia; the British military mission stayed on into the mid-1960s, Egyptian troops had fought in the south before 1956, Libya supplied arms and money from 1969 and was directly involved in combat by 1970, and Uganda permitted the southern fighters to operate on its own territory and fed them between 1965 and 1969. The southern side was more heterogeneous: the guerrilla movement that grew out of the 1955 Torit mutiny took shape from 1963 and took the name Anyanya, a Ma'di word meaning snake venom, which later became the label for the whole war; there were also the Azania Liberation Front, active between 1965 and 1970, and a scatter of local armed groups. From 1969 Israel too was involved directly, supplying arms to the southern movement and posting military advisers. Geographically the fighting was concentrated in the southern provinces of Equatoria (Torit, Juba, Yei, Maridi), Upper Nile and Bahr al Ghazal, country of swamps, savanna and rain forest threaded by the White Nile and its tributaries.
people: 這場內戰的關鍵人物分屬三個世代。殖民地時期主持南部善後的英方總督亞歷山大·諾克斯·赫爾姆，在兵變爆發時正夾在英國撤出與蘇丹獨立的交接點上；北方則由蘇丹第一任總理伊斯梅爾·阿扎里領銜，他主張北方精英應主導新國家，這一立場使南北裂痕在獨立後立即固化。1958年推翻阿扎里內閣的是陸軍參謀長布里格adier易卜拉欣·阿布德（Ibrahim Abboud），他在1958年政變後執掌軍政，直到1964年10月20日夜間卡土穆大學保安部隊突擊一場以「南部蘇丹問題」為題的研討會，引發全國性罷工與遊行，即所謂「十月革命」，阿布德被迫辭職。1969年5月25日加法爾·尼米里再度以政變上台，立即解散政黨，此後三年蘇丹政局在軍人與共產黨之間反覆折騰，1971年7月共產黨短暫執政後又被反共派推翻。南方領袖幾經更替：阿格雷·雅登（Aggrey Jaden）是分離主義運動最早推舉的領袖，1969年因內部爭議出走；同年戈登·穆爾塔特·梅延（Gordon Muortat Mayen）獲一致推選為南方領袖，此後因不願接受以迪卡人為核心的統一領導而與部分赤道派交惡。1971年，前南方軍官出身的約瑟夫·拉古（Joseph Lagu）在以色列協助下發動政變推翻梅延，把各路游擊隊統一在「南方蘇丹解放運動」（SSLM）之下，成為這場戰爭中第一個擁有統一指揮架構、並以建立獨立國家為公開目標的組織。以色列方面的指揮者為大衛·本-烏齊爾（David Ben-Uziel），他自1969年起在南方培訓部隊並協調軍援。值得一提的還有德籍顧問羅夫爾·史泰納（Rolf Steiner），他自1969年起秘密輔助南方武裝，1971年在坎帕拉被捕、押回卡土穆受審，最初被判死刑，在西德政府施壓下改判，服刑三年後獲釋。1964年的學生運動中，哈桑·圖拉比（Hassan al-Turabi）首次以學生領袖身分嶄露頭角，此後成為蘇丹伊斯蘭主義的政治核心人物。1972年3月的《亞的斯亞貝巴協定》，則是在埃塞俄比亞皇帝海爾·塞拉西見證下簽訂的。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities of the war belong to three generations. Governor-general Alexander Knox Helm, who managed southern affairs during the colonial period, was caught at the handover point between the British withdrawal and Sudanese independence when the mutiny broke out. In the north, Ismail al-Azhari, Sudan's first prime minister, led the claim that the northern elite should dominate the new state, and that stance fixed the north-south split immediately after independence. Brigadier Ibrahim Abboud, chief of the general staff, overthrew al-Azhari's government in the 1958 coup and then ran the country until the evening of 20 October 1964, when a security force raided a seminar on the problem of the southern Sudan at the University of Khartoum and set off nationwide strikes and demonstrations, the so-called October Revolution, which forced his resignation. On 25 May 1969 Gaafar Nimeiry seized power by coup again, dissolved the parties at once, and the next three years saw the Sudanese establishment oscillate between soldiers and communists, with a brief communist administration after the July 1971 coup before the anti-communists pushed Nimeiry back into control. The southern leadership changed hands repeatedly: Aggrey Jaden was the first man the separatist movement put forward and left the movement in 1969 over internal disputes; that same year Gordon Muortat Mayen was elected unanimously as leader of the south, and from then on he fell out with part of the Equatorian faction because a Dinka would not accept a Dinka at the head of a unified command. In 1971 Joseph Lagu, a former southern army lieutenant, staged a coup against Mayen with Israeli help and united the guerrilla bands under the Southern Sudan Liberation Movement, the first organisation in the war to have a single command structure and an openly declared goal of an independent state. On the Israeli side the commander was David Ben-Uziel, who trained southern forces and coordinated the arms deliveries from 1969. Worth noting too is the German adviser Rolf Steiner, who secretly assisted the southern fighters from 1969, was arrested in Kampala in 1971 and deported to Khartoum for trial, was sentenced to death at first, had the sentence commuted under pressure from the West German government, and was released after three years in prison. In the student movement of 1964 Hassan al-Turabi first appeared as a student leader and would go on to become the political core of Sudanese Islamism. The Addis Ababa Agreement of March 1972 was signed under the witnessing eye of the Emperor of Ethiopia, Haile Selassie.
kits: 卡面這具M3斯圖亞特輕型坦克，是英軍在二戰中最先接收的美製輕型坦克，車體自1941年3月量產至1943年10月，主武器為一門37公厘M5砲（後改用加長的M6），輔以五挺口徑.30-06的布侖M1919A4機槍；首上裝甲38公厘、首下44公厘、砲盾51公厘、砲塔側面38公厘、車體側後各25公厘，乘員三人而砲塔僅容二人，越野行程約一百二十一公里。絕大多數車體裝空冷星形汽油機Continental W-670，另有一千四百九十六輛改用Guiberson T-1020柴油機；後出的M5與M5A1改用雙Cadillac V8自動變速箱，連同底盤衍生的M8 75公厘自行榴彈砲在內，M3與M5系總產逾兩萬五千輛。就本場戰爭而言必須老實說明：蘇丹軍隊從未成建制配發M3，1955至1972年間在南部作戰的裝甲力量是英制輪式裝甲車與裝甲列車，輔以吉普車與卡車。M3的意義在於它恰好代表同一時代、同一殖民軍力體系中「以輕型裝甲承擔偵察與護路」的角色，而它在二戰後確實以類似身分出現在其他地區的內戰與反叛亂戰場：英軍在印尼獨立戰爭中把M3A1與M3A3用到1946年，葡軍1970年代初在安哥拉以三輛加拿大援助的M5A1執行車隊護衛與救援，1969年薩爾瓦多入侵宏都拉斯時以M3充當主戰車，1965年印巴戰爭中巴基斯坦亦有M3建制。南方武裝真正用得上的，是英軍在蘇丹國防軍時期留下的家底：李-恩菲爾德步槍、司登式衝鋒槍、布侖式輕機槍、維克斯重機槍、二吋與八十一公厘迫擊砲，以及繳獲的彈藥與軍用卡車；北軍除上述英制武器外另有裝甲列車與裝甲巡邏車，1960年代末起才逐步獲得蘇聯提供的航空裝備與通用武器。
kitsEn: The M3 Stuart on the card face was the first American light tank the British Army took into service in the Second World War; the hull was produced from March 1941 to October 1943, the main weapon a 37 mm M5 gun, later replaced by the longer M6, backed by five .30-06 Browning M1919A4 machine guns; armour was 38 mm on the upper front hull, 44 mm on the lower front, 51 mm on the mantlet, 38 mm on the turret sides and 25 mm on hull sides and rear; the crew was three with only two in the turret, and cross-country range was about 121 kilometres. The overwhelming majority carried the air-cooled radial Continental W-670 petrol engine, with 1,496 vehicles using the Guiberson T-1020 diesel; the later M5 and M5A1 adopted twin Cadillac V8 engines and a Hydramatic automatic transmission, and including the M8 75 mm howitzer motor carriage built on the same chassis, total M3 and M5 production ran past 25,000 vehicles. It has to be said plainly that the Sudanese army was never issued the M3 as a formation: the armour that fought in the south between 1955 and 1972 was British wheeled armoured cars and armoured trains, supported by jeeps and trucks. The significance of the M3 is that it represents precisely the role of the light tank in the same era and the same colonial military system, that of reconnaissance and convoy escort; after the war it did play comparable parts in civil wars and counter-insurgencies elsewhere: British forces used M3A1s and M3A3s in the Indonesian national revolution until 1946, the Portuguese army employed three Canadian-aid M5A1s in Angola in the early 1970s for convoy escort and recovery, El Salvador used the M3 as its main battle tank when it invaded Honduras in 1969, and Pakistan fielded the M3 in the 1965 Indo-Pakistani war. What the southern fighters actually used was the legacy the British left behind in the Sudan Defence Force: Lee-Enfield rifles, Sten submachine guns, Bren light machine guns, Vickers heavy machine guns, 2-inch and 81 mm mortars, and captured ammunition and military trucks. On the northern side the same British weapons were joined by armoured trains and armoured reconnaissance cars, and only towards the end of the 1960s did Soviet aircraft equipment and small arms begin to arrive.
tactics: 這場內戰的戰術面貌，是在沒有正面戰線的廣袤南部逐步改寫的。1955年8月18日，赤道軍團第二連在托里特起兵，數日內擴散至朱巴、耶伊與馬里迪，隨即被從北部調來的部隊鎮壓；倖存者散入鄉間，與零散游擊隊匯合，1955至1963年因此被稱為「游擊求生存」的階段——支撐這段時期的不過是數十名前蘇丹國防軍的軍官與士官，裝備極少，組織鬆散，與一般劫掠無異。北軍的戰術則是縱隊加據點：以公路為軸，步兵沿土路推進，在城鎮、渡口與橋樑設卡駐防，並以裝甲車、裝甲列車與飛機巡邏護路；1955年之後即以一個步兵旅常駐赤道省，視需要增援，師旅級兵力在雨季難以展開，攻勢多集中在旱季。南方武裝充分利用雨季、河網、沼澤與叢林，白天分散、夜間集結，襲擊哨所與補給車隊，破壞道路橋梁，得手後迅速撤回境外；1965年起阿札尼亞解放陣線等武裝加入後，襲擊縱深與目標轉向城鎮，對北軍城防與交通線的壓力明顯上升。與此同時，戰局被北方的政治變化牽動：1964年十月革命使軍人政權失去控制，1965至1966年間北方政黨衝突與南方陣營分裂交錯，1969年尼米里政變後北軍收緊控制，卻同時捲入代理人戰爭；南方則在以色列協助下於1971年統一號令。1972年3月《亞的斯亞貝巴協定》能夠達成，靠的不是戰場勝負，而是世界基督教教會理事會與全非基督教會議多年斡旋所建立的雙方互信，談判地點選在亞的斯亞貝巴，由埃塞俄比亞皇帝見證。
tacticsEn: The tactical character of the war was gradually rewritten across a vast southern theatre with no front line. On 18 August 1955 No. 2 Company of the Equatoria Corps mutinied at Torit; the mutiny spread within days to Juba, Yei and Maridi and was then suppressed by troops sent down from the north. The survivors scattered into the countryside and merged with bands of guerrillas, and the period from 1955 to 1963 came to be known as one of guerrilla survival: it was sustained by no more than a score of former Sudan Defence Force officers and non-commissioned officers, poorly armed, badly organised, scarcely removed from banditry. Northern doctrine was column plus strongpoint. The army moved along the roads, infantry pushing up the dirt tracks, establishing posts at towns, fords and bridges, and patrolling the lines of communication with armoured cars, armoured trains and aircraft; from 1955 one infantry brigade was stationed permanently in Equatoria Province and was reinforced as required, and divisional strength could not easily be deployed in the rains, so offensives were mostly confined to the dry season. The southern fighters exploited the rains, the river network, the swamps and the forest, dispersing by day and concentrating at night, raiding outposts and supply convoys, cutting roads and bridges and withdrawing quickly across the border afterwards. From 1965, with the arrival of the Azania Liberation Front and similar groups, the depth of the raids and the choice of targets shifted towards the towns, and the pressure on northern communications and garrison towns rose sharply. All the while the war was pulled by political change in the north: the October Revolution of 1964 deprived the military government of control, party fighting in the north and the split in the southern camp crossed each other in 1965 and 1966, and after Nimeiry's coup of 1969 the government tightened its grip while being drawn into a proxy war. The south, with Israeli help, finally got a single command in 1971. The Addis Ababa Agreement of March 1972 was not won on the field but built on the mutual trust created by years of mediation by the World Council of Churches and the All Africa Conference of Churches, negotiated in Addis Ababa under the witnessing Ethiopian emperor.
data: 可查數字大致勾勒出這場戰爭的規模，細目則多有缺漏。時間上，戰爭自1955年8月18日起，至1972年3月27日《亞的斯亞貝巴協定》為止，前後近十七年。兵力方面，蘇丹武裝部隊在1955年約六千至七千人，1971年底增至約三萬六千人；南方阿尼亞尼亞武裝的規模，各家說法由六千至一萬二千人不等，至1960年代末約達一萬八千人。英軍顧問團規模、烏干達與利比亞援助的批次數量、南方游擊隊的武器繳獲總數，均無可靠統計。部隊編制上，蘇丹全軍共四個步兵旅，其中一個自1955年起常駐赤道省，境內另有地方防衛隊與民兵，1969年後北軍還以空軍支援南方作戰。戰術層面的數字更少：1955至1963年的游擊階段全靠數十名前蘇丹國防軍軍官與士官維持，具體小組人數與活動範圍史載有限。傷亡方面，各家統計差異極大，可確認者僅是作戰人員的損失逾十萬人，民間人口的傷亡數字不屬本站記錄範圍。距離與補給線方面，烏干達邊境是最重要的補給與撤退通道，托里特、朱巴、馬里迪等城鎮間的公路則是北軍推進的主軸，至於每次戰鬥的逐日傷亡、具體推進距離與各師展開序列，現有記載多付闕如，只能以概略推想。
dataEn: The available figures sketch the scale of the war, though the detail is thin. In time: the war ran from 18 August 1955 to 27 March 1972, when the Addis Ababa Agreement was signed, a span of nearly seventeen years. In men: the Sudanese Armed Forces numbered about 6,000 to 7,000 in 1955 and had grown to some 36,000 by late 1971; the strength of the Anyanya is given variously at 6,000 to 12,000, rising to around 18,000 by the late 1960s. There are no reliable statistics for the size of the British military mission, for the batches of aid from Uganda and Libya, or for the total volume of weapons captured by the southern guerrillas. In organisation: the army had four infantry brigades in all, one of them stationed in Equatoria Province from 1955 onwards, with a locally raised defence force and militia alongside, and from 1969 the northern side added air support for operations in the south. At tactical level the numbers are thinner still: the guerrilla phase of 1955 to 1963 rested on a score of former Sudan Defence Force officers and non-commissioned officers, and the size of individual bands and the ground they covered are barely recorded. In losses the estimates differ wildly; what can be confirmed is that more than 100,000 combatants were killed, while the figures for deaths among the civilian population fall outside the scope of this site. In distance and lines of communication: the Ugandan border was the single most important supply and withdrawal route, and the roads linking Torit, Juba and Maridi formed the main axis of northern advance, while the day-by-day casualties, the exact distances covered and the deployment sequences of individual brigades are largely unrecorded and can only be reconstructed in outline.
cause: 第一次蘇丹內戰的起因，可從殖民分治、獨立後的權力結構與直接導火線三層來看。最底層是殖民時期的制度安排：英國與埃及王國共管北部蘇丹，而南蘇丹在行政上長期與北部分治，1956年獨立的政治運動把兩地合併成一個國家時，未曾徵詢南部少數族群的政治領袖。獨立之後，北方精英在伊斯梅爾·阿扎里的旗幟下掌握主導權，南部在中央議會中代表稀少，又同時是種族與宗教上的少數，其資源與教育差距成為不滿的來源，直接引爆1955年8月的兵變：一名南部國會議員受審，加上據稱內容失實、要求北方官員鎮壓南部人的一封電報，使赤道軍團第二連在托里特起兵。導火線雖小，深層原因卻是長期積累的不平等。戰爭之所以拖長並擴大，還因為兩個外部變數：一是北方政局在1960年代反覆震盪，1964年十月革命、1966年的分裂聯盟與1969年政變接連削弱了政府的軍事控制力，南方武裝得以在雨季間隙裡擴張；二是代理人競爭，烏干達、利比亞與以色列先後介入，把原本的內部衝突變成冷戰的邊疆戰場，而北方自身的政黨分裂也讓每一次停火與談判都隨時可能破裂。史載有限之處，在於南方各派系之間的權力分配細節與早期游擊的實際戰術，多只能依西方觀察者的記述與後來的口述史推想。
causeEn: The origins of the First Sudanese Civil War can be read on three levels: the colonial partition, the structure of power after independence, and the immediate spark. At the bottom lies the institutional arrangement of the colonial period. Britain and the Kingdom of Egypt jointly governed northern Sudan, while the south was administratively separated from the north for decades, and when the independence movement merged the two into a single country in 1956 it did so without consulting the political leaders of the southern minority. After independence the northern elite, under the banner of Ismail al-Azhari, took control of the new state; the south had few representatives in the central parliament and was at once a racial and a religious minority, and the gap in resources and in education became the substance of the grievance. That grievance produced the mutiny of August 1955: the trial of a southern member of the national assembly, and an allegedly false telegram urging northern administrators in the south to repress the southerners, together put No. 2 Company of the Equatoria Corps on its feet at Torit. The spark was small; the cause was a long accumulation of inequality. The war dragged on and widened for two further reasons. First, the northern political situation convulsed throughout the 1960s: the October Revolution of 1964, the splintered coalition of 1966 and the coup of 1969 each deprived the government of military control, and the southern fighters expanded in the gaps between the rains. Second, proxy competition: Uganda, Libya and Israel entered in turn, converting what had been an internal conflict into a cold war frontier, while the factionalism of the northern parties themselves meant that every ceasefire and every negotiation could break apart at any moment. The record is thin on the internal distribution of power among the southern factions and on the actual tactics of the early guerrillas, and has to be reconstructed from Western observers' accounts and later oral history.
impact: 1972年3月27日簽訂的《亞的斯亞貝巴協定》，是這場內戰留下的制度遺產：南部成立「南部區域政府」，設區域議會與行政委員會，享有相當程度的內部自治，北方的政策重心由消滅分離主義轉為治理一個自治單位。協定同時埋下新的矛盾——南部不得擁有獨立的武裝部隊，其防衛與治安仍由北方軍隊負責，自治與軍事壟斷並存，註定難以長久。從更大的格局看，這場戰爭是冷戰時期非洲代理人戰爭的樣板：烏干達、利比亞、以色列與蘇丹本土的政黨一齊在南部角力，武器與顧問跨境流動，後來南部非洲與安哥拉、衣索比亞的角力都沿用同一模式。軍事技術上，這是一場「輪式裝甲車對叢林游擊」的對照：北軍投入裝甲列車、裝甲巡邏車與空中支援，仍未能清剿缺乏重裝備的游擊隊，說明後殖民國家的常備軍在缺乏社會基礎與後勤縱深時難以對付小隊游擊；南方則靠境外補給與政治組織取代了兵種優勢。裝備史上，這段時期也標誌著英制殖民地軍械體系的退場：二戰留下的大量輕型裝備仍在亞洲、非洲與中美洲的內戰現場發揮餘熱，戰爭的形態則由制式軍備的對決轉為正規軍對游擊隊的長期消耗。代價方面，據引述有逾十萬名作戰人員陣亡，數十萬人被迫離家（民間人口的傷亡數字不屬本站記錄範圍）。最重要的長期後果是：1970年代中期以後北方加強干預，1983年5月阿科博守軍兵變引發第二次蘇丹內戰，二十二年後南蘇丹終於獨立；換言之，第一次蘇丹內戰並未終結南北問題，只是把它推延。
impactEn: The Addis Ababa Agreement signed on 27 March 1972 is the institutional legacy of the war: a Southern Regional Government was created, with a Regional Assembly and an Executive Council serving as its legislative and executive organs, enjoying a considerable measure of internal autonomy, and the focus of northern policy shifted from suppressing separatism to administering an autonomous unit. At the same time the agreement planted a new contradiction. The south was not permitted to have its own armed forces; its defence and internal security remained in the hands of the northern army, and autonomy existing side by side with military monopoly could not last. On the larger stage the war became a template for cold war proxy conflict in Africa: Uganda, Libya, Israel and Sudan's own parties all competed in the south, weapons and advisers crossing the borders freely, and the same pattern was later used in southern Africa, Angola and Ethiopia. In military terms it was a contest between wheeled armour and bush guerrillas: the north committed armoured trains, armoured reconnaissance cars and air support and still failed to clear guerrillas short of heavy equipment, showing that a post-colonial regular army without social roots or logistical depth cannot defeat small-unit insurgency; the south substituted overseas supply and political organisation for armoured weight. In the history of equipment the period also marks the retirement of the British colonial ordnance system: the vast stock of light matériel left over from the Second World War was still at work in the civil wars of Asia, Africa and Central America, while the form of war itself shifted from a clash of regular formations to a long attrition between standing armies and guerrillas. As to costs, more than 100,000 combatants are recorded as killed and hundreds of thousands were driven from their homes; figures for deaths among the civilian population fall outside the scope of this site. The most important long-term consequence is this: after renewed northern intervention in the mid-1970s, the mutiny of the garrison at Akobo in May 1983 triggered the Second Sudanese Civil War, and South Sudan was independent twenty-two years later. The first Sudanese civil war did not settle the north-south question; it deferred it.
result: 結局是僵局加妥協，而不是任何一方的勝利。十七年戰爭之後，北方未能消滅南方武裝，南方也未能攻下卡土穆；1972年3月27日，在埃塞俄比亞皇帝海爾·塞拉西見證下，蘇丹政府與南方代表於亞的斯亞貝巴簽署協定，規定南部區域自治、成立區域議會與行政委員會，戰爭至此在法律上終止，時間上正是官方史家慣用的終點。交戰雙方都沒有達成原初目標：北方的國家統一訴求被換成有條件的自治，南方的獨立目標則被壓後數十年。協定後的一段時間裡，蘇丹出現相對平穩與重建，南部地區學校、醫療與行政逐步恢復，鐵路與港口的南北運輸也重新運轉，北部與南部的關係卻始終緊張，軍隊部署、資源分配與代表席位的爭議不斷累積，終於在1983年重新引爆成第二次蘇丹內戰。回到卡面：M3斯圖亞特輕型坦克從未在蘇丹的戰線上出現，它的真正戰史在二戰北非、印度支那與太平洋戰場，以及戰後的印尼、安哥拉、中美洲與印巴衝突；把它放在這張卡上，是要標示這場內戰所屬的技術世代——以輕型裝甲與輪式裝甲車執行偵察護路、而游擊隊以叢林與跨境補給維持存亡的世代，而蘇丹南部正是這種不對稱對抗最漫長的一處試驗場。
resultEn: The outcome was stalemate and compromise rather than victory for either side. After seventeen years the north had failed to destroy the southern armed groups and the south had failed to take Khartoum; on 27 March 1972, with the Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie witnessing, the Sudanese government and southern representatives signed the agreement in Addis Ababa, providing for regional autonomy in the south and the creation of a Regional Assembly and an Executive Council. The war ended at law on that date, which is also the date conventionally taken by official historians as its close. Neither side achieved its original aim: the northern claim to a unified state was exchanged for conditional autonomy, and the southern goal of independence was deferred by decades. In the years after the agreement Sudan enjoyed a period of relative calm and reconstruction, with schools, medical services and administration in the south gradually restored and the rail and river transport between north and south working again; yet the relationship remained tense, and disputes over troop deployments, the distribution of resources and the number of parliamentary seats accumulated until they blew up again in 1983 as the Second Sudanese Civil War. Back to the card: the M3 Stuart never appeared on a front line in Sudan. Its real war history lies in North Africa, Burma and the Pacific during the Second World War, and afterwards in Indonesia, Angola, Central America and the Indo-Pakistani conflict. Putting it on this card marks the technological generation to which the war belonged: an era in which light tanks and wheeled armoured cars performed reconnaissance and convoy escort while guerrillas stayed alive through the forest and across the border, and the southern Sudan proved to be the longest testing ground of that asymmetric contest.
